title: Tanzanian Crab Curry
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Mchuzi wa Kaa — fresh Zanzibar crabs in a rich coconut milk and tamarind curry. The most communal seafood dish of the coast — messy, fun, and extraordinarily flavourful.
longDesc: Crab curry is the most communal seafood dish of the Tanzanian coast — eaten with hands, shells cracked at the table, sauce mopped with chapati. The mess is half the point.
ingredients: 4 fresh whole crabs (500g each) — cleaned and quartered
steps: Clean and quarter crabs. Crack claws.
Cook onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, spices.
Add crab pieces. Stir to coat.
Add coconut milk and tamarind. Simmer covered 20—25 minutes.
Crab is ready when bright red throughout.
chefTips: Crab turns bright red when cooked.
cookingScience: Crab shell contains astaxanthin bound to protein — heat denatures the protein, releasing astaxanthin which turns the shell bright red. This colour change is the cooking indicator.
sustainabilityTips: Zanzibar mud crabs from local tidal flat fishermen.
culturalNote: Crab curry is the most social seafood dish of coastal Tanzania — the meal eaten together, shells cracked, sauce shared, voices raised.
